sentence_stem: I had my car repaired yesterday,
correct_completion: so it runs much better now.
full_sentence: I had my car repaired yesterday, so it runs much better now.
acceptable_variants: so I can drive it safely.

options.text: so it runs much better now.

options.why_wrong: 'Had ... repaired' means someone else did the work for me, so this contradicts the causative structure.

options.text: although it runs much better now.
options.why_wrong: 'Although' introduces a contrast, which does not fit the logical result of the repair.

options.text: the car was repaired by me.
options.why_wrong: This passive form says I did the repair, which contradicts the meaning of 'had my car repaired'.

grammar_focus: Causative 'have something done' with a result clause
explanation: The causative 'have something done' means someone else performs the action for the subject. Turkish speakers often use a simple past verb here, because Turkish has a separate suffix for causation and can express 'had repaired' without a helper verb.
translation: Arabamı dün tamir ettirdim, bu yüzden artık çok daha iyi çalışıyor.
